title: Hardness of a Probabilistic Machine Acceptance Language
statement: For every code $c$ of a binary-choice probabilistic Turing machine, the language whose strings encode triples $(\alpha,x,t)$ as $\langle\alpha,\langle x,1^t\rangle\rangle$ and for which the machine decoded from $\alpha$ accepts $x$ within $t$ steps with probability at least $2/3$ is hard for $\mathsf{BPP}$ under polynomial-time many-one reductions. Here $\mathsf{BPP}$ is the class of languages decidable by a finite probabilistic Turing machine in polynomial time with acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on members and at most $1/3$ on nonmembers.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a code for a probabilistic Turing machine
